[b]January 18, 2028: Izmir the Great[/b]

Orhan Izmýr, the shah of 33 million people and a booming industry worth billions, and yet, he was perplexed. There had been whispers of a coup to the north by effeminate males; the jurists had begun to whisper about whether the prophet had given permission for them to exist, and the orthodox had threatened to convene in Rosenmarkke if the matter was not solved.

Yet Orhan did not think as they thought, in prophecy, or in canon; he thought as a businessman thinks, was it stable? Would it bring more money into Yzakastan? 

Moving from his desk where he was seated, his fingertips brushing the finely carved mahogany, he turned on the record player that sat next to the desk, a delicious sounding Makam began to play, the notes oozing out of the speakers like an enchanting melody.

Orhan began to dance to the music as he thought.  He would summon the speaker and prelate of the senate and the Chamber of the People.  Yes, that is what he would do, and they would chat over tea and biscuits about the situation in the North. 

Moving swiftly, he made haste and dialed the chief steward, calling him to summon the two men for a meeting that afternoon. Vyzmir would not stay silent if silence was dangerous; they knew what silence could do if left untended.
